# 28063 Federal Register / Vol. 84, No. 116 / Monday, June 17, 2019 / Notices 

DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES National Institutes of Health Prospective Grant of Exclusive Patent License: Lutetium-177 Radiotherapeutics Against Somatostatin-Receptor Expressing Neuroendocrine Tumors AGENCY : National Institutes of Health, HHS.  

> ACTION

: Notice.  

> SUMMARY

: The National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute (NHLBI), National Institutes of Health, Department of Health and Human Services, is contemplating amending an existing license to include a exclusive patent license to Molecular Targeting Technologies, Inc. (MTTI); a Delaware corporation, with its principle place of business in West Chester, Pennsylvania, to practice the inventions embodied in the patent application listed in the  

> SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION

section of this notice.  

> DATES

: Only written comments and/or applications for a license which are received by the NHLBI Office of Technology Transfer and Development July 2, 2019 will be considered.  

> ADDRESSES

: Requests for copies of the patent applications, inquiries, and comments relating to the contemplated exclusive patent license should be directed to: Michael Shmilovich, Esq., Senior Licensing and Patent Manager, 31 Center Drive, Room 4A29, MSC2479, Bethesda, MD 20892–2479, phone number 301–435–5019, or shmilovm@ mail.nih.gov.  

> SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION

: The following and all continuing U.S. and foreign patents/patent applications thereof are the intellectual properties to be licensed under the prospective agreement to MTTI:                     

> NIH ref No. Patent No. or patent application No. Filing date Title E–150–2016–0–US–01 .. 62/333,427 .............. May 9, 2019 ............ Chemical Conjugates of Evans Blue Derivatives and Their Use as Ra-diotherapy and Imaging Agents. E–150–2016–0–PCT–02 PCT/US2017/ 031696. May 9, 2017 ............ Chemical Conjugates of Evans Blue Derivatives and Their Use as Ra-diotherapy and Imaging Agents. E–150–2016–0–CN–03 .. 201780029003X ...... November 9, 2018 .. Chemical Conjugates of Evans Blue Derivatives and Their Use as Ra-diotherapy and Imaging Agents. E–150–2016–0–EP–04 .. 17796666.0 ............. November 12, 2018 Chemical Conjugates of Evans Blue Derivatives and Their Use as Ra-diotherapy and Imaging Agents. E–150–2016–0–JP–05 ... 2018–558662 .......... November 8, 2018 .. Chemical Conjugates of Evans Blue Derivatives and Their Use as Ra-diotherapy and Imaging Agents. E–150–2016–0–US–06 .. 16/099,488 .............. November 7, 2018 .. Chemical Conjugates of Evans Blue Derivatives and Their Use as Ra-diotherapy and Imaging Agents.

The patent rights in these inventions have been assigned to the Government of the United States of America. The prospective patent license will be granted worldwide and limited to the extent that the above referenced patents or patent applications cover lutetium-177 radiotherapeutics for somatostatin-receptor expressing neuroendocrine tumors. The invention pertains to a radiotherapeutic against neuroendocrine tumors that express somatostatin receptor. Radionuclide therapies directed against tumors that express somatostatin receptors (SSTRs) have proven effective for the treatment of advanced, low- to intermediate-grade neuroendocrine tumors. The subject radiotherapeutic covered by the subject patent estate includes a somatostatin (SST) peptide derivative like octreotate (TATE), conjugated to an Evans Blue (EB) analog, and further chelated via DOTA to therapeutic radionuclide. The EB analog reversibly binds to circulating serum albumin and improves the pharmacokinetics of SST peptide derivatives and reduce peptide-receptor radionuclide therapy toxicity. EB analog conjugated to octreotate (EB-DOTATATE) has been shown by the inventors to provide reversible albumin binding in vivo and extended half-life in circulation. When EB-TATE is slowly released into the tumor microenvironment, tumor uptake and internalization into SSTR positive tumors resulted in delivery of radioactive particles and tumor cell killing. EB-TATE displayed significantly more favorable pharmacokinetics than TATE alone by achieving higher tumor to non-tumor penetration as evidenced by positron emission tomography. This notice is made in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 209 and 37 CFR part 404. The prospective exclusive patent license will be royalty bearing and may be granted unless within fifteen (15) days from the date of this published notice, the NHLBI receives written evidence and argument that establishes that the grant of the license would not be consistent with the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 209 and 37 CFR part 404. Complete applications for a license in the prospective field of use that are timely filed in response to this notice will be treated as objections to the grant of the contemplated exclusive patent license. Comments and objections submitted to this notice will not be made available for public inspection and, to the extent permitted by law, will not be released under the Freedom of Information Act, 

5 U.S.C. 552. Dated: June 3, 2019. 

> Michael A. Shmilovich,
> Senior Licensing and Patenting Manager, National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, Office of Technology Transfer and Development.

(‘‘Tailored’’), located in Potomac, MD.

Radionuclide therapies directed against tumors that express somatostatin receptors (SSTRs) have proven effective for the treatment of advanced, low- to intermediate-grade neuroendocrine tumors. The subject radiotherapeutic covered by the subject patent estate includes a somatostatin (SST) peptide derivative like octreotate (TATE), conjugated to an Evans Blue (EB) analog, and further chelated via DOTA to therapeutic radionuclide. The EB analog reversibly binds to circulating serum albumin and improves the pharmacokinetics of SST peptide derivatives and reduce peptide-receptor radionuclide therapy toxicity. EB analog conjugated to octreotate (EB-DOTATATE) has been shown by the inventors to provide reversible albumin binding in vivo and extended half-life in circulation. When EB-TATE is slowly released into the tumor microenvironment, tumor uptake and internalization into SSTR positive tumors resulted in delivery of radioactive particles and tumor cell killing. ## Abstract

[18 F]F-AraG is a clinical-stage PET tracer in immuno-oncology that accumulates in activated T cells and tissues with high mitochondrial biogenesis. Characterizing its distribution in individuals without malignancy is essential for interpreting immunometabolic states relevant to cancer biology. **Methods:** Twenty adults without active malignancy underwent a single [18 F]F-AraG PET/CT scan, with tracer uptake assessed in relation to clinical history, medications, and demographic and physiologic factors. **Results:** Bilateral brown adipose tissue activation was identified in 3 participants receiving potentially brown adipose tissue–activating medications, in the absence of cold exposure or fasting. One showed elevated vertebral bone marrow uptake, previously linked to poor survival in immune checkpoint inhibitor–treated lung cancer. One of 2 participants with breast implants showed asymmetric periimplant uptake. Posterior pulmonary uptake occurred in a subset of participants, often with prior respiratory conditions and thoracic lymph node uptake. **Conclusion:** Whole-body [18 F]F-AraG PET captures diverse immunometabolic activity in individuals without malignancy, reflecting systemic processes that may influence cancer and treatment outcomes.

Journal of Nuclear Medicine October 2026, jnumed.126.272735; DOI: https://doi.org/10.2967/jnumed.126.272735

## Abstract

Evidence supporting the efficacy and safety of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas derives mainly from small, single-center studies. The French national multicenter MELUTE study aimed to consolidate these data using a standardized regimen within a compassionate-use program approved by a national multidisciplinary tumor board. **Methods:** In this retrospective multicenter cohort study, patients with refractory meningiomas treated with [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in 18 French centers between July 2022 and December 2024 were included. Treatment consisted of 7.4 GBq every 8 wk for up to 4 cycles. Clinical data (demographics, histologic World Health Organization grade [WHO], prior treatments, number of cycles, toxicity, progression, survival status as of October 1, 2025) were collected. Baseline [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET and brain MRI scans obtained before and after treatment were centrally reviewed. The primary endpoint was 6-mo progression-free survival (PFS) assessed using volumetric Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology Group criteria. Secondary endpoints were PFS, overall survival (OS), and safety. **Results:** Sixty-nine patients were included (mean age, 65.1 ± 13.2 y; 52% female): 13 WHO grade 1, 42 WHO grade 2, 8 WHO grade 3, and 6 without histology. Most had prior surgery (86%) or radiotherapy (93%); 32% received prior systemic therapy. Twelve patients (17%) did not complete 4 cycles; only one discontinuation was toxicity-related. Six-month PFS was 70% (95% CI, 58.7–80.4%). Median PFS was 14.6 mo (95% CI, 13.3–18.5 mo), and median OS was 27.6 mo (95% CI, 24.2 mo to not reached). Grade 3 adverse events, mainly lymphopenia, occurred in 16%. Meningioma WHO grade independently predicted PFS, whereas higher Karnofsky performance status and corticosteroid use were protective; worse OS was associated with higher baseline tumor growth rate and prior systemic therapy. **Conclusion:** MELUTE demonstrates promising efficacy and favorable safety of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas with limited therapeutic options.

*   [multicenter study](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/keyword/multicenter-study)

Refractory meningiomas, defined as tumors that are resistant to or not amenable to surgery or radiotherapy, are rare but probably underestimated ([1](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-1)) and are associated with poor clinical outcomes ([2](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-2)). Radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) represents a relatively novel therapeutic approach in this setting and enables targeted irradiation of meningioma lesions through the use of radiolabeled somatostatin receptor (SSTR) ligands combined with radionuclides delivering high linear energy transfer ([3](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-3)). SSTR ligands are expressed in meningiomas ([4](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-4)), including higher-grade tumors ([5](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-5)). According to a meta-analysis ([6](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-6)) and the largest retrospective series reported to date ([7](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-7)), RPT with radiolabeled SSTR ligands has demonstrated promising efficacy, with 6-mo progression-free survival (PFS-6) rates of approximately 60% in refractory meningiomas. These results exceed current Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology Group (RANO) benchmarks used to evaluate the efficacy of systemic therapies in recurrent meningiomas, defined as a PFS-6 of 49% for refractory World Health Organization (WHO) grade 2 and 3 meningiomas (PFS-6 benchmark at 67% in WHO grade 1 meningiomas) ([8](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-8)).

However, the available evidence is primarily based on studies with limited sample sizes and with heterogeneous RPT regimens combining a mixture of DOTATOC/TATE radioligand radiolabeled with 177 Lu or 90 Y and for which most are monocentric ([3](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-3)). In France, national health authorities approved a compassionate-use program (CUP) for [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas in April 2022 ([https://ansm.sante.fr/uploads/2022/04/06/20220406-decision-ansm-cpc-lutathera.pdf](https://ansm.sante.fr/uploads/2022/04/06/20220406-decision-ansm-cpc-lutathera.pdf)). Within this framework, prescriptions of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE must be validated by the national OMEGA multidisciplinary tumor board for refractory meningiomas. This CUP provides a unique opportunity to retrospectively collect multicenter data on [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy delivered according to a standardized treatment regimen. To further assess the potential of SSTR ligand–based RPT in refractory meningiomas, this study proposes a centralized review of MRI and PET imaging data from French nuclear medicine centers that administered [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE under the CUP. Such data are highly anticipated by the medical community, particularly given the time required to obtain results from ongoing prospective studies currently under development ([9](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-9)).

The French national multicenter MELUTE (MEningiomas and LUTEtium) study aimed to consolidate findings from previous single-center studies by evaluating the efficacy and safety of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy in patients treated within the CUP framework, using PFS-6 as the primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints include median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS), safety, and tolerability. Factors associated with therapeutic responses were also evaluated.

## MATERIALS AND METHODS

### Study Population

Patients with refractory meningiomas treated in 18 French centers that participated in the MELUTE study, who received the first cycle of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE between July 2022 and December 2024, were retrospectively included. Treatment decisions were made within the framework of the CUP and validated by the national OMEGA (group of the RENOCLIP-LOC network, approved by the National Cancer Institute) multidisciplinary tumor board for refractory meningiomas, which includes at least one neuro-oncologist, one neurosurgeon, one radiation oncologist, and one nuclear medicine physician. Details of inclusion criteria are provided in the Supplemental Data file (available at [http://jnm.snmjournals.org](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/)). The flowchart for patient selection is available in [Figure 1](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#F2).

### RPT Regimen

All included patients received a standardized RPT regimen consisting of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE (7.4 GBq every 8 wk, up to 4 cycles, with half-injected activities in case of toxicity), in accordance with the CUP. Positively charged amino acids (l-lysine or l-arginine) were coinfused during each treatment cycle to reduce renal radiation exposure, as recommended ([10](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-10)). Corticosteroid therapy was permitted during treatment cycles when clinically indicated.

### Clinical, Pathologic, and Biologic Data

All anonymized data were collected locally by a principal investigator who fulfilled a standardized electronic case report form (eCRF). PFS-6 was calculated from clinico-radiologic data available at 6 mo after the first cycle of RPT according to volumetric RANO criteria ([11](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-11)) with a centralized review. Global PFS was also calculated from the start of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy to disease progression reported in the eCRF. OS was calculated from the first treatment cycle to death from any cause reported in the eCRF.

Pathologic data included WHO grade according to the WHO classification of meningiomas ([12](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-12)). Toxicity was assessed using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0. Both clinical and biologic adverse events (from complete blood count, liver and kidney function tests) were recorded and graded from 1 to 4 for each treatment cycle.

### Imaging Data

Pretreatment [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET scans and brain MRI scans obtained before and after treatment were collected for centralized analysis using a dedicated imaging platform (Archimed platform, [https://www.cic-it-nancy.fr/fr/plateforme-archimed/](https://www.cic-it-nancy.fr/fr/plateforme-archimed/)). MRI and PET were centrally reviewed by 2 readers with a consensual analysis using the application of volumetric RANO criteria for meningiomas ([11](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-11)), enabling direct assessment of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE’s effect on tumor volume growth rates (TGRs) on MRI and extraction of SUV-derived parameters in PET (details in supplemental materials). Complete, partial, and minor responses and stable disease according to RANO criteria ([11](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-11)) were considered favorable responses and were used to determine PFS-6. Progressive disease was classified as disease progression. Death from any cause was also classified as disease progression.

For patients with additional imaging available, at least one MRI before baseline (prebaseline MRI) and one MRI at the end of RPT were collected. TGRs were calculated before treatment (between the prebaseline MRI and baseline MRI, V0) and during treatment (between baseline MRI and the last available MRI, V1) ([13](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-13)). Details of calculation and results of TGRs are provided in the supplemental materials.

### Statistical Analysis

All details on statistical analyses are provided in supplemental material. Statistical analyses were performed using R software version 4.5.2 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing).

## RESULTS

### Patient Characteristics

Seventy-four patients who were treated under the CUP for the defined period participated in the MELUTE study; 5 were secondarily excluded because 3 patients lacked baseline MRI or 6-mo follow-up scans and 2 patients had surgery during the RPT regimen ([Fig. 1](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#F2)). The final cohort comprised 69 patients (mean age, 65.1 ± 13.2 y; 36 females, 52%, median of 1 [interquartile range, 1–4] supracentimetric meningioma lesions per patient), including 13 WHO grade 1, 42 WHO grade 2, 8 WHO grade 3, and 6 unclassified meningiomas (patients with no biopsy/surgery).

With respect to pretherapeutic [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET images, 57 (83%) patients underwent a whole-body PET scan (of whom 52 [91%] had meningioma uptake superior or equal to that in the liver ([10](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-10))). Among these patients, 6 (11%, 1 WHO grade 1, 3 WHO grade 2, 1 WHO grade 3, and 1 unclassified meningioma) were identified as having confirmed or highly suggestive lesions of extracranial metastatic localization.

Prior treatments included surgery in 59 (86%) patients, radiotherapy in 64 (93%, 53.2 mo [interquartile range, 37.1–87.8 mo] before RPT) patients, surgery and radiotherapy in 54 (78%) patients, and systemic therapy in 22 (32%) patients (of whom 17 had combination of surgery and radiotherapy, 1 had combination with surgery alone, and 4 had combination with radiotherapy alone). Twelve patients (17%) did not complete all 4 treatment cycles (1 patient received only 1 cycle, 9 patients received 2 cycles, and 2 patients received 3 cycles): 8 because of disease progression, 2 were patient decision, 1 was due to radionuclide toxicity (grade 3 neutropenia), and 1 because of an intercurrent event unrelated to RPT (iatrogenic acute hepatitis not related to RPT). The mean cumulative administered activity was 26.548 ± 5.535 GBq, with significantly lower cumulative activity in WHO grade 3 meningiomas (_P_ = 0.02; Supplemental Table 1). Detailed patient characteristics are presented in [Table 1](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#T1) and Supplemental Table 1.

### PFS-6

The mean interval between the first treatment cycle and the 6-mo MRI was 7.6 ± 2.0 mo. Twenty-one patients (30%) experienced disease progression according to RANO criteria within 6 mo: 4 based on clinical deterioration (3 with concomitant volumetric progression), 3 due to the appearance of new lesions (2 with associated volumetric progression), and 19 with volumetric progression alone. Overall PFS-6 was 70% (95% CI, 58.7–80.4%). Among the 48 patients with favorable responses, 47 had stable diseases and 1 achieved a minor response. PFS-6 rates were 85%, 62%, and 88% for WHO grades 1, 2, and 3 meningiomas, respectively. To note, in the 5 patients for whom pretherapeutic [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET uptake in meningioma was not superior or equal to that in the liver, PFS-6 was determined at 60%. PFS-6 was 100% (6 stable diseases) in the 6 patients with extracranial metastases (no other PET imaging was retrieved to evaluate the extracranial disease response). ### PFS and OS

PFS data were available for 62 patients and OS data for 65 patients related to patients lost in follow-up. The mean follow-up duration was 24.9 ± 7.8 mo (45 progressions, 73% of patients and 24 deaths, 37% of patients during follow-up). Median PFS was 14.6 mo (95% CI, 13.3–18.5 mo) overall, with 20.0 mo (95% CI, 13.9 mo to not reached), 13.8 mo (95% CI, 12.1–17.7 mo), and 13.0 mo (95% CI, 3.9 mo to not reached) for WHO grades 1, 2, and 3 meningiomas, respectively. Median OS was 27.6 mo (95% CI, 24.2 mo to not reached) overall, with 26.4 mo (95% CI, 21.8 mo to not reached) for WHO grade 1, not reached (95% CI, 24.2 mo to not reached) for grade 2, and 13.0 mo (95% CI, 12.2 mo to not reached) for grade 3 meningiomas. ### Toxicity

Eleven patients (16%) experienced at least one grade 3 adverse event. Among these, 9 patients (13%) experienced hematologic toxicities, 2 patients (3%) neuromotor toxicities, and 1 patient (1%) asthenia. Only 1 patient (1%) experienced 2 grade 3 adverse events (asthenia and lymphopenia). The majority of grade 3 adverse events were lymphopenia (8 patients, 12%). Two patients (3%) required hospitalization during their treatment because of the worsening or onset of motor deficit, in a context of known tumor progression.

Permanent discontinuation of treatment due to RPT was necessary in only 1 patient (1%) because of grade 3 neutropenia. A dose reduction during cycles was required in 2 patients (3%): because of grade 2 thrombocytopenia for the first patient and because of abnormal liver function tests not related to RPT for the second patient. [Table 2](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#T2) summarizes grade 3 or higher adverse events.

### Factors Associated with Therapeutic Responses

In multivariate Cox models adjusted for age and sex, WHO meningioma grade was independently associated with PFS, whereas higher Karnofsky performance status and corticosteroid use during RPT were protective factors ([Table 3](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#T3)). For OS, rapid initial TGR and prior systemic therapy were associated with worse outcomes ([Table 3](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#T3)). Supplemental Figure 1 presents Kaplan–Meier curves related to individual identified prognostic factors in multivariate Cox analyses ([Table 3](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#T3)).

## DISCUSSION

The MELUTE study is a retrospective national multicenter study evaluating the efficacy and tolerance of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy in refractory meningiomas using a homogeneous treatment regimen. All patients included were referred for [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy according to the French CUP and after validation by the national multidisciplinary tumor board, representing real-world population. By integrating centralized imaging review and volumetric assessment, our study provides robust data supporting RPT in refractory meningiomas.

The primary objective of this study was to determine PFS-6 in patients with refractory meningiomas treated with [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE, thereby confirming the promising results reported in multiple smaller, monocentric retrospective studies with heterogeneous regimens ([6](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-6)). PFS-6 was chosen as the primary endpoint as it is the most representative outcome recommended by the RANO group for assessing treatment efficacy in refractory meningiomas ([8](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-8)). In our cohort, PFS-6 (70%) slightly exceeded the 61% reported in a meta-analysis of 111 patients ([6](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-6)), the 58% reported in a recent retrospective study ([7](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-7)), or even the 50% reported in a preliminary prospective study of 14 patients using exclusively RPT with [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE ([14](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-14)). Similarly, median PFS and OS, used as primary endpoints in [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE prospective trials in refractory meningiomas ([9](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-9)), were longer in our population than those reported in both retrospective and prospective series (median PFS, <10 mo; OS, ∼22 mo) ([7](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-7),[14](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-14),[15](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-15)). Our study included meningiomas of all WHO grades, consistent with previous reports. However, patients were selected by a national multidisciplinary tumor board, which may have excluded patients with poorer overall status and ensured the inclusion of lesions with significant uptake on pretherapeutic [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET (≥1.7-fold SUV peak of contralateral meninges and, for most of them, equal/greater than liver uptake, resulting in a median SUV max of 16 for included patients) ([10](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-10),[16](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-16)), which could explain our better treatment efficacy. These results highlight the importance of pretreatment multidisciplinary assessment to identify patients most likely to benefit from RPT. Interestingly, PFS-6 for WHO grade 3 meningiomas was unexpectedly high (88%) in a limited group sample of 8 patients, probably related to the fact that patients included were younger than those with other meningioma WHO grades (Supplemental Table 1), though median PFS and OS in this subgroup remained short (13.0 mo), consistent with their generally poor prognosis. This benefit of RPT in WHO grade 3 meningiomas is also related to the fact that the multidisciplinary board has selected WHO grade 3 meningiomas with favorable profile (expression of SSTR receptors in pretherapeutic PET, relative low initial meningioma volume; Supplemental Table 1) for the national CUP. The predominant response observed across the cohort was disease stabilization according to RANO criteria ([11](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-11)) (98% of nonprogressive cases), confirming previous reports ([6](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-6),[7](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-7),[14](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-14),[15](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-15)). The best minor response observed (2% of nonprogressive cases) is presented in [Figure 2](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#F3).

Tolerability of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy was excellent, as previously reported ([6](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-6)). Only 16% of patients experienced grade 3 or greater adverse events, primarily lymphopenia, a well-known effect of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy ([6](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-6)). Only one patient discontinued therapy because of reversible grade 3 neutropenia; no other treatment interruptions were required because of adverse events related to the RPT.

Factors associated with treatment response were also evaluated. Meningioma WHO grade was an independent predictor of PFS, consistent with prior studies ([4](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-4),[7](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-7)). Karnofsky performance status was also prognostic for survival outcomes, as expected. Notably, prior systemic therapy (everolimus, bevacizumab, or octreotide) was associated with poorer OS, likely reflecting more advanced disease, as recently reported ([16](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-16)). A high TGR before RPT was also an independent risk factor of OS. All of these prognostic factors confirm that patients with refractory meningiomas should be initially selected during a multidisciplinary tumor board that includes a nuclear medicine physician before being referred to RPT, particularly to exclude patients with poorer clinical status, advanced disease, or rapid progressive meningiomas, at risk of not benefiting from [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy. Surprisingly, corticosteroid therapy administered during RPT, despite its relative contraindication in this setting ([10](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-10)), was associated with improved PFS. This unexpected finding should be interpreted with caution and does not imply a causal relationship. Although corticosteroids may modulate the tumor microenvironment, the precise mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear and warrant further targeted investigation. No pretherapeutic PET parameters correlated with treatment response, consistent with other reports ([7](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-7),[16](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-16)). Prior work suggests that low tumor absorbed dose, the real dose administered to the meningioma tumor resulting from dosimetry analyses and those different from the total intravenous injected activity, may limit observable dose–response relationships ([17](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-17)).

A strength of this study is the centralized application of volumetric RANO criteria for meningiomas ([11](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-11)), enabling direct assessment of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE’s effect on TGRs. Using the methodology of Graillon et al. ([18](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-18),[19](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-19)), we observed a median TGR reduction of −17% per 6 mo in all WHO grade meningiomas, with interestingly higher TGR decreases in more aggressive WHO grades 2 and 3 meningiomas. Details on TGR measurements during [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy are provided in the supplemental materials, Supplemental Figures 2 and 3, and Supplemental Table 3, ([18](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-18)).

This study has limitations inherent to its retrospective design, including reliance on data provided by multiple centers and lack of PET harmonization across centers. Notably, regarding the retrospective design, the MRI part of the PFS-6 calculation (7.6 ± 2.0 mo from the first RPT cycle to the 6-mo MRI) could have underestimated the real PFS-6. Although outcomes of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy appear favorable compared with those reported for systemic therapies in refractory meningiomas ([8](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-8)), such comparisons remain indirect and should be interpreted with caution. Nevertheless, keeping in mind that our population was selected as previously mentioned, these national multicenter data, using a homogeneous treatment regimen and a centralized imaging data analyses, are valuable given the time required to obtain results from ongoing large-scale prospective trials ([9](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-9)).

## CONCLUSION

The MELUTE study confirms the promising efficacy and safety of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy in a selected population of refractory meningiomas. Further prospective studies are warranted to strengthen the evidence supporting [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy in this population ([3](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-3),[9](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-9)), considering prognostic factors associated with therapeutic responses identified in the current study.

The retrospective French MELUTE multicenter study was approved by the Comité d’Éthique CHRU de Nancy, registered on ClinicalTrials.gov ([NCT06255249](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/lookup/external-ref?link_type=CLINTRIALGOV&access_num=NCT06255249&atom=%2Fjnumed%2Fearly%2F2026%2F10%2F15%2Fjnumed.126.272735.atom)), and informed consent was waived.

## DISCLOSURE

This study was supported by Advanced Accelerator Applications, a Novartis company, by a grant covering human resources to collect the data. No other potential conflict of interest relevant to this article was reported.

#### KEY POINTS

**QUESTION:** Does a standardized regimen of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE provide effective and safe disease control in patients with refractory meningiomas?

**PERTINENT FINDINGS:** In this retrospective multicenter cohort of 69 patients, PFS-6 reached 70%, with a median PFS of 14.6 mo and an OS of 27.6 mo. Treatment was generally well tolerated, with grade 3 adverse events in 16%, mainly lymphopenia, and very few discontinuations because of toxicity.

**IMPLICATIONS FOR PATIENT CARE:** [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE appears to be a promising and well-tolerated therapeutic option for patients with refractory meningiomas who have limited alternatives.

## ACKNOWLEDGMENTS

We want to acknowledge the Nancyclotep Imaging Platform (Clinical Research Department) and the CIC-IT (CHRU Nancy) for their support.

Journal of Nuclear Medicine October 2026, jnumed.126.272735; DOI: https://doi.org/10.2967/jnumed.126.272735

## Abstract

Evidence supporting the efficacy and safety of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas derives mainly from small, single-center studies. The French national multicenter MELUTE study aimed to consolidate these data using a standardized regimen within a compassionate-use program approved by a national multidisciplinary tumor board. **Methods:** In this retrospective multicenter cohort study, patients with refractory meningiomas treated with [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in 18 French centers between July 2022 and December 2024 were included. Treatment consisted of 7.4 GBq every 8 wk for up to 4 cycles. Clinical data (demographics, histologic World Health Organization grade [WHO], prior treatments, number of cycles, toxicity, progression, survival status as of October 1, 2025) were collected. Baseline [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET and brain MRI scans obtained before and after treatment were centrally reviewed. The primary endpoint was 6-mo progression-free survival (PFS) assessed using volumetric Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology Group criteria. Secondary endpoints were PFS, overall survival (OS), and safety. **Results:** Sixty-nine patients were included (mean age, 65.1 ± 13.2 y; 52% female): 13 WHO grade 1, 42 WHO grade 2, 8 WHO grade 3, and 6 without histology. Most had prior surgery (86%) or radiotherapy (93%); 32% received prior systemic therapy. Twelve patients (17%) did not complete 4 cycles; only one discontinuation was toxicity-related. Six-month PFS was 70% (95% CI, 58.7–80.4%). Median PFS was 14.6 mo (95% CI, 13.3–18.5 mo), and median OS was 27.6 mo (95% CI, 24.2 mo to not reached). Grade 3 adverse events, mainly lymphopenia, occurred in 16%. Meningioma WHO grade independently predicted PFS, whereas higher Karnofsky performance status and corticosteroid use were protective; worse OS was associated with higher baseline tumor growth rate and prior systemic therapy. **Conclusion:** MELUTE demonstrates promising efficacy and favorable safety of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas with limited therapeutic options.

*   [peptide receptor radionuclide therapy](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/keyword/peptide-receptor-radionuclide-therapy)
*   [PRRT](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/keyword/prrt)
*   [[177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/keyword/177lulu-dotatate)
*   [somatostatin receptor imaging](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/keyword/somatostatin-receptor-imaging)
*   [multicenter study](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/keyword/multicenter-study)

Refractory meningiomas, defined as tumors that are resistant to or not amenable to surgery or radiotherapy, are rare but probably underestimated ([1](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-1)) and are associated with poor clinical outcomes ([2](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-2)). Radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) represents a relatively novel therapeutic approach in this setting and enables targeted irradiation of meningioma lesions through the use of radiolabeled somatostatin receptor (SSTR) ligands combined with radionuclides delivering high linear energy transfer ([3](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-3)). SSTR ligands are expressed in meningiomas ([4](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-4)), including higher-grade tumors ([5](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-5)). According to a meta-analysis ([6](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-6)) and the largest retrospective series reported to date ([7](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-7)), RPT with radiolabeled SSTR ligands has demonstrated promising efficacy, with 6-mo progression-free survival (PFS-6) rates of approximately 60% in refractory meningiomas. These results exceed current Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology Group (RANO) benchmarks used to evaluate the efficacy of systemic therapies in recurrent meningiomas, defined as a PFS-6 of 49% for refractory World Health Organization (WHO) grade 2 and 3 meningiomas (PFS-6 benchmark at 67% in WHO grade 1 meningiomas) ([8](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-8)).

However, the available evidence is primarily based on studies with limited sample sizes and with heterogeneous RPT regimens combining a mixture of DOTATOC/TATE radioligand radiolabeled with 177 Lu or 90 Y and for which most are monocentric ([3](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-3)). In France, national health authorities approved a compassionate-use program (CUP) for [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas in April 2022 ([https://ansm.sante.fr/uploads/2022/04/06/20220406-decision-ansm-cpc-lutathera.pdf](https://ansm.sante.fr/uploads/2022/04/06/20220406-decision-ansm-cpc-lutathera.pdf)). Within this framework, prescriptions of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE must be validated by the national OMEGA multidisciplinary tumor board for refractory meningiomas. This CUP provides a unique opportunity to retrospectively collect multicenter data on [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy delivered according to a standardized treatment regimen. To further assess the potential of SSTR ligand–based RPT in refractory meningiomas, this study proposes a centralized review of MRI and PET imaging data from French nuclear medicine centers that administered [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE under the CUP. Such data are highly anticipated by the medical community, particularly given the time required to obtain results from ongoing prospective studies currently under development ([9](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-9)).

The French national multicenter MELUTE (MEningiomas and LUTEtium) study aimed to consolidate findings from previous single-center studies by evaluating the efficacy and safety of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy in patients treated within the CUP framework, using PFS-6 as the primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints include median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS), safety, and tolerability. Factors associated with therapeutic responses were also evaluated.

## MATERIALS AND METHODS

### Study Population

Patients with refractory meningiomas treated in 18 French centers that participated in the MELUTE study, who received the first cycle of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE between July 2022 and December 2024, were retrospectively included. Treatment decisions were made within the framework of the CUP and validated by the national OMEGA (group of the RENOCLIP-LOC network, approved by the National Cancer Institute) multidisciplinary tumor board for refractory meningiomas, which includes at least one neuro-oncologist, one neurosurgeon, one radiation oncologist, and one nuclear medicine physician. Details of inclusion criteria are provided in the Supplemental Data file (available at [http://jnm.snmjournals.org](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/)). The flowchart for patient selection is available in [Figure 1](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#F2).

### RPT Regimen

All included patients received a standardized RPT regimen consisting of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE (7.4 GBq every 8 wk, up to 4 cycles, with half-injected activities in case of toxicity), in accordance with the CUP. Positively charged amino acids (l-lysine or l-arginine) were coinfused during each treatment cycle to reduce renal radiation exposure, as recommended ([10](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-10)). Corticosteroid therapy was permitted during treatment cycles when clinically indicated.

### Clinical, Pathologic, and Biologic Data

All anonymized data were collected locally by a principal investigator who fulfilled a standardized electronic case report form (eCRF). PFS-6 was calculated from clinico-radiologic data available at 6 mo after the first cycle of RPT according to volumetric RANO criteria ([11](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-11)) with a centralized review. Global PFS was also calculated from the start of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy to disease progression reported in the eCRF. OS was calculated from the first treatment cycle to death from any cause reported in the eCRF.

Pathologic data included WHO grade according to the WHO classification of meningiomas ([12](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-12)). Toxicity was assessed using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0. Both clinical and biologic adverse events (from complete blood count, liver and kidney function tests) were recorded and graded from 1 to 4 for each treatment cycle.

### Imaging Data

Pretreatment [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET scans and brain MRI scans obtained before and after treatment were collected for centralized analysis using a dedicated imaging platform (Archimed platform, [https://www.cic-it-nancy.fr/fr/plateforme-archimed/](https://www.cic-it-nancy.fr/fr/plateforme-archimed/)). MRI and PET were centrally reviewed by 2 readers with a consensual analysis using the application of volumetric RANO criteria for meningiomas ([11](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-11)), enabling direct assessment of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE’s effect on tumor volume growth rates (TGRs) on MRI and extraction of SUV-derived parameters in PET (details in supplemental materials). Complete, partial, and minor responses and stable disease according to RANO criteria ([11](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-11)) were considered favorable responses and were used to determine PFS-6. Progressive disease was classified as disease progression. Death from any cause was also classified as disease progression.

For patients with additional imaging available, at least one MRI before baseline (prebaseline MRI) and one MRI at the end of RPT were collected. TGRs were calculated before treatment (between the prebaseline MRI and baseline MRI, V0) and during treatment (between baseline MRI and the last available MRI, V1) ([13](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-13)). Details of calculation and results of TGRs are provided in the supplemental materials.

### Statistical Analysis

All details on statistical analyses are provided in supplemental material. Statistical analyses were performed using R software version 4.5.2 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing).

## RESULTS

### Patient Characteristics

Seventy-four patients who were treated under the CUP for the defined period participated in the MELUTE study; 5 were secondarily excluded because 3 patients lacked baseline MRI or 6-mo follow-up scans and 2 patients had surgery during the RPT regimen ([Fig. 1](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#F2)). The final cohort comprised 69 patients (mean age, 65.1 ± 13.2 y; 36 females, 52%, median of 1 [interquartile range, 1–4] supracentimetric meningioma lesions per patient), including 13 WHO grade 1, 42 WHO grade 2, 8 WHO grade 3, and 6 unclassified meningiomas (patients with no biopsy/surgery).

With respect to pretherapeutic [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET images, 57 (83%) patients underwent a whole-body PET scan (of whom 52 [91%] had meningioma uptake superior or equal to that in the liver ([10](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-10))). Among these patients, 6 (11%, 1 WHO grade 1, 3 WHO grade 2, 1 WHO grade 3, and 1 unclassified meningioma) were identified as having confirmed or highly suggestive lesions of extracranial metastatic localization.

Prior treatments included surgery in 59 (86%) patients, radiotherapy in 64 (93%, 53.2 mo [interquartile range, 37.1–87.8 mo] before RPT) patients, surgery and radiotherapy in 54 (78%) patients, and systemic therapy in 22 (32%) patients (of whom 17 had combination of surgery and radiotherapy, 1 had combination with surgery alone, and 4 had combination with radiotherapy alone). Twelve patients (17%) did not complete all 4 treatment cycles (1 patient received only 1 cycle, 9 patients received 2 cycles, and 2 patients received 3 cycles): 8 because of disease progression, 2 were patient decision, 1 was due to radionuclide toxicity (grade 3 neutropenia), and 1 because of an intercurrent event unrelated to RPT (iatrogenic acute hepatitis not related to RPT). The mean cumulative administered activity was 26.548 ± 5.535 GBq, with significantly lower cumulative activity in WHO grade 3 meningiomas (_P_ = 0.02; Supplemental Table 1). Detailed patient characteristics are presented in [Table 1](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#T1) and Supplemental Table 1.

TABLE 1.

Patient Characteristics

### PFS-6

The mean interval between the first treatment cycle and the 6-mo MRI was 7.6 ± 2.0 mo. Twenty-one patients (30%) experienced disease progression according to RANO criteria within 6 mo: 4 based on clinical deterioration (3 with concomitant volumetric progression), 3 due to the appearance of new lesions (2 with associated volumetric progression), and 19 with volumetric progression alone. Overall PFS-6 was 70% (95% CI, 58.7–80.4%). Among the 48 patients with favorable responses, 47 had stable diseases and 1 achieved a minor response. PFS-6 rates were 85%, 62%, and 88% for WHO grades 1, 2, and 3 meningiomas, respectively. To note, in the 5 patients for whom pretherapeutic [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET uptake in meningioma was not superior or equal to that in the liver, PFS-6 was determined at 60%. PFS-6 was 100% (6 stable diseases) in the 6 patients with extracranial metastases (no other PET imaging was retrieved to evaluate the extracranial disease response). Representative PET/MR images of the patient with a minor response are shown in [Figure 2](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#F3).

Treatment consisted of 7.4 GBq every 8 wk for up to 4 cycles. Clinical data (demographics, histologic World Health Organization grade [WHO], prior treatments, number of cycles, toxicity, progression, survival status as of October 1, 2025) were collected. Baseline [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET and brain MRI scans obtained before and after treatment were centrally reviewed. The primary endpoint was 6-mo progression-free survival (PFS) assessed using volumetric Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology Group criteria. Secondary endpoints were PFS, overall survival (OS), and safety. **Results:** Sixty-nine patients were included (mean age, 65.1 ± 13.2 y; 52% female): 13 WHO grade 1, 42 WHO grade 2, 8 WHO grade 3, and 6 without histology. Most had prior surgery (86%) or radiotherapy (93%); 32% received prior systemic therapy. Twelve patients (17%) did not complete 4 cycles; only one discontinuation was toxicity-related. Six-month PFS was 70% (95% CI, 58.7–80.4%). Median PFS was 14.6 mo (95% CI, 13.3–18.5 mo), and median OS was 27.6 mo (95% CI, 24.2 mo to not reached). Grade 3 adverse events, mainly lymphopenia, occurred in 16%. Meningioma WHO grade independently predicted PFS, whereas higher Karnofsky performance status and corticosteroid use were protective; worse OS was associated with higher baseline tumor growth rate and prior systemic therapy. **Conclusion:** MELUTE demonstrates promising efficacy and favorable safety of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas with limited therapeutic options.

*   [PRRT](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/keyword/prrt)
*   [[177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/keyword/177lulu-dotatate)
*   [somatostatin receptor imaging](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/keyword/somatostatin-receptor-imaging)
*   [multicenter study](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/keyword/multicenter-study)

Refractory meningiomas, defined as tumors that are resistant to or not amenable to surgery or radiotherapy, are rare but probably underestimated ([1](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-1)) and are associated with poor clinical outcomes ([2](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-2)). Radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) represents a relatively novel therapeutic approach in this setting and enables targeted irradiation of meningioma lesions through the use of radiolabeled somatostatin receptor (SSTR) ligands combined with radionuclides delivering high linear energy transfer ([3](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-3)). SSTR ligands are expressed in meningiomas ([4](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-4)), including higher-grade tumors ([5](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-5)). According to a meta-analysis ([6](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-6)) and the largest retrospective series reported to date ([7](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-7)), RPT with radiolabeled SSTR ligands has demonstrated promising efficacy, with 6-mo progression-free survival (PFS-6) rates of approximately 60% in refractory meningiomas. These results exceed current Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology Group (RANO) benchmarks used to evaluate the efficacy of systemic therapies in recurrent meningiomas, defined as a PFS-6 of 49% for refractory World Health Organization (WHO) grade 2 and 3 meningiomas (PFS-6 benchmark at 67% in WHO grade 1 meningiomas) ([8](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-8)).

However, the available evidence is primarily based on studies with limited sample sizes and with heterogeneous RPT regimens combining a mixture of DOTATOC/TATE radioligand radiolabeled with 177 Lu or 90 Y and for which most are monocentric ([3](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-3)). In France, national health authorities approved a compassionate-use program (CUP) for [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas in April 2022 ([https://ansm.sante.fr/uploads/2022/04/06/20220406-decision-ansm-cpc-lutathera.pdf](https://ansm.sante.fr/uploads/2022/04/06/20220406-decision-ansm-cpc-lutathera.pdf)). Within this framework, prescriptions of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE must be validated by the national OMEGA multidisciplinary tumor board for refractory meningiomas. This CUP provides a unique opportunity to retrospectively collect multicenter data on [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy delivered according to a standardized treatment regimen. To further assess the potential of SSTR ligand–based RPT in refractory meningiomas, this study proposes a centralized review of MRI and PET imaging data from French nuclear medicine centers that administered [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE under the CUP. Such data are highly anticipated by the medical community, particularly given the time required to obtain results from ongoing prospective studies currently under development ([9](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-9)).

The French national multicenter MELUTE (MEningiomas and LUTEtium) study aimed to consolidate findings from previous single-center studies by evaluating the efficacy and safety of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy in patients treated within the CUP framework, using PFS-6 as the primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints include median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS), safety, and tolerability. Factors associated with therapeutic responses were also evaluated.

## MATERIALS AND METHODS

### Study Population

Patients with refractory meningiomas treated in 18 French centers that participated in the MELUTE study, who received the first cycle of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE between July 2022 and December 2024, were retrospectively included. Treatment decisions were made within the framework of the CUP and validated by the national OMEGA (group of the RENOCLIP-LOC network, approved by the National Cancer Institute) multidisciplinary tumor board for refractory meningiomas, which includes at least one neuro-oncologist, one neurosurgeon, one radiation oncologist, and one nuclear medicine physician. Details of inclusion criteria are provided in the Supplemental Data file (available at [http://jnm.snmjournals.org](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/)). The flowchart for patient selection is available in [Figure 1](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#F2).

### RPT Regimen

All included patients received a standardized RPT regimen consisting of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE (7.4 GBq every 8 wk, up to 4 cycles, with half-injected activities in case of toxicity), in accordance with the CUP. Positively charged amino acids (l-lysine or l-arginine) were coinfused during each treatment cycle to reduce renal radiation exposure, as recommended ([10](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-10)). Corticosteroid therapy was permitted during treatment cycles when clinically indicated.

### Clinical, Pathologic, and Biologic Data

All anonymized data were collected locally by a principal investigator who fulfilled a standardized electronic case report form (eCRF). PFS-6 was calculated from clinico-radiologic data available at 6 mo after the first cycle of RPT according to volumetric RANO criteria ([11](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-11)) with a centralized review. Global PFS was also calculated from the start of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy to disease progression reported in the eCRF. OS was calculated from the first treatment cycle to death from any cause reported in the eCRF.

Pathologic data included WHO grade according to the WHO classification of meningiomas ([12](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-12)). Toxicity was assessed using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0. Both clinical and biologic adverse events (from complete blood count, liver and kidney function tests) were recorded and graded from 1 to 4 for each treatment cycle.

### Imaging Data

Pretreatment [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET scans and brain MRI scans obtained before and after treatment were collected for centralized analysis using a dedicated imaging platform (Archimed platform, [https://www.cic-it-nancy.fr/fr/plateforme-archimed/](https://www.cic-it-nancy.fr/fr/plateforme-archimed/)). MRI and PET were centrally reviewed by 2 readers with a consensual analysis using the application of volumetric RANO criteria for meningiomas ([11](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-11)), enabling direct assessment of [177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE’s effect on tumor volume growth rates (TGRs) on MRI and extraction of SUV-derived parameters in PET (details in supplemental materials). Complete, partial, and minor responses and stable disease according to RANO criteria ([11](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-11)) were considered favorable responses and were used to determine PFS-6. Progressive disease was classified as disease progression. Death from any cause was also classified as disease progression.

For patients with additional imaging available, at least one MRI before baseline (prebaseline MRI) and one MRI at the end of RPT were collected. TGRs were calculated before treatment (between the prebaseline MRI and baseline MRI, V0) and during treatment (between baseline MRI and the last available MRI, V1) ([13](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-13)). Details of calculation and results of TGRs are provided in the supplemental materials.

### Statistical Analysis

All details on statistical analyses are provided in supplemental material. Statistical analyses were performed using R software version 4.5.2 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing).

## RESULTS

### Patient Characteristics

Seventy-four patients who were treated under the CUP for the defined period participated in the MELUTE study; 5 were secondarily excluded because 3 patients lacked baseline MRI or 6-mo follow-up scans and 2 patients had surgery during the RPT regimen ([Fig. 1](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#F2)). The final cohort comprised 69 patients (mean age, 65.1 ± 13.2 y; 36 females, 52%, median of 1 [interquartile range, 1–4] supracentimetric meningioma lesions per patient), including 13 WHO grade 1, 42 WHO grade 2, 8 WHO grade 3, and 6 unclassified meningiomas (patients with no biopsy/surgery).

With respect to pretherapeutic [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET images, 57 (83%) patients underwent a whole-body PET scan (of whom 52 [91%] had meningioma uptake superior or equal to that in the liver ([10](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#ref-10))). Among these patients, 6 (11%, 1 WHO grade 1, 3 WHO grade 2, 1 WHO grade 3, and 1 unclassified meningioma) were identified as having confirmed or highly suggestive lesions of extracranial metastatic localization.

Prior treatments included surgery in 59 (86%) patients, radiotherapy in 64 (93%, 53.2 mo [interquartile range, 37.1–87.8 mo] before RPT) patients, surgery and radiotherapy in 54 (78%) patients, and systemic therapy in 22 (32%) patients (of whom 17 had combination of surgery and radiotherapy, 1 had combination with surgery alone, and 4 had combination with radiotherapy alone). Twelve patients (17%) did not complete all 4 treatment cycles (1 patient received only 1 cycle, 9 patients received 2 cycles, and 2 patients received 3 cycles): 8 because of disease progression, 2 were patient decision, 1 was due to radionuclide toxicity (grade 3 neutropenia), and 1 because of an intercurrent event unrelated to RPT (iatrogenic acute hepatitis not related to RPT). The mean cumulative administered activity was 26.548 ± 5.535 GBq, with significantly lower cumulative activity in WHO grade 3 meningiomas (_P_ = 0.02; Supplemental Table 1). Detailed patient characteristics are presented in [Table 1](http://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/early/2026/10/15/jnumed.126.272735#T1) and Supplemental Table 1.

TABLE 1.

Patient Characteristics

### PFS-6

The mean interval between the first treatment cycle and the 6-mo MRI was 7.6 ± 2.0 mo. Twenty-one patients (30%) experienced disease progression according to RANO criteria within 6 mo: 4 based on clinical deterioration (3 with concomitant volumetric progression), 3 due to the appearance of new lesions (2 with associated volumetric progression), and 19 with volumetric progression alone. Overall PFS-6 was 70% (95% CI, 58.7–80.4%). Among the 48 patients with favorable responses, 47 had stable diseases and 1 achieved a minor response. PFS-6 rates were 85%, 62%, and 88% for WHO grades 1, 2, and 3 meningiomas, respectively. To note, in the 5 patients for whom pretherapeutic [68 Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET uptake in meningioma was not superior or equal to that in the liver, PFS-6 was determined at 60%. PFS-6 was 100% (6 stable diseases) in the 6 patients with extracranial metastases (no other PET imaging was retrieved to evaluate the extracranial disease response). ## **Technetium-99m oxidronate (HDP)**

**Approved Use:**Skeletal imaging agent used to demonstrate areas of altered osteogenesis in adult and pediatric patients

**Dose:**
*   Adult: 15 mCi (range = 10 - 20 mCi)
*   Pediatric: 0.20 mCi/kg (range = 0.20 - 0.35 mCi/kg)

**Brand Name:**TechneScan™HDP

**Manufacturer:** Curium

**[Package Insert](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/hdp-pi_dec_2018.pdf)**

**How Supplied:**
*   5 vial kit (NDC: 69945-091-20)
*   30 vial kit (NDC: 69945-091-40)

[Letter from Manufacturer](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/hdp_vial_change_cust_letter_with_pi_06-16-2020.pdf) June 2020 (packaging change)

**Clinical Guidelines:**​
*   [SNMMI Procedure Standard for Bone Scintigraphy V4.0(2024)](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/bone_scintigraphy_updated2024.pdf)

## **Technetium-99m oxidronate (HDP)**

**Approved Use:**Skeletal imaging agent used to demonstrate areas of altered osteogenesis in adult and pediatric patients

**Dose:**
*   Adult: 15 mCi (range = 10 - 20 mCi)
*   Pediatric: 0.20 mCi/kg (range = 0.20 - 0.35 mCi/kg)

**Brand Name:**TechneScan™HDP

**Manufacturer:** Curium

**[Package Insert](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/hdp-pi_dec_2018.pdf)**

**How Supplied:**
*   5 vial kit (NDC: 69945-091-20)
*   30 vial kit (NDC: 69945-091-40)

[Letter from Manufacturer](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/hdp_vial_change_cust_letter_with_pi_06-16-2020.pdf) June 2020 (packaging change)

**Clinical Guidelines:**​
*   [SNMMI Procedure Standard for Bone Scintigraphy V4.0(2024)](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/bone_scintigraphy_updated2024.pdf)
*   [ACR-ACNM-SNMMI-SPR Practice Parameter for the Performance of Skeletal Scintigraphy (2021)](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/skeletal-scint_2021.pdf)

## **Technetium-99m macroaggregated albumin (MAA)**

**Approved Use:**
*   Lung imaging agent which may be used as an adjunct in the evaluation of pulmonary perfusion in adults and pediatric patients
*   Aid in the evaluation of peritoneovenous (LeVeen) shunt patency

**Dose:**
*   **​**Lung imaging (Adult): 1 - 4 mCi; 200,000 - 700,000 particles (350,000 suggested)
*   Lung imaging (pediatric): 25 - 50 µCi/kg (usual dose is 30 µCi/kg); see package insert
*   Lung imaging (newborn): 200 - 500 µCi; see package insert
*   LeVeen shunt patency: 1 - 3 mCi

**[MAA Particle Calculator](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/maa-particle-calcs.html)**

* * *

**Manufacturer:**Jubilant Radiopharma

**[Package Insert](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/maa_pi_oct_2017.pdf)**

**Storage:**Refrigerate AFTER reconstitution

**How Supplied:**30 vial kit

**NDC #:**65174-270-30

​**Particle Count:**
*   3- 8 million particles per vial
*   Certificate of particle count and "simplified reconstitution recommendations" included with each lot.

## **Technetium-99m macroaggregated albumin (MAA)**

**Approved Use:**
*   Lung imaging agent which may be used as an adjunct in the evaluation of pulmonary perfusion in adults and pediatric patients
*   Aid in the evaluation of peritoneovenous (LeVeen) shunt patency

**Dose:**
*   **​**Lung imaging (Adult): 1 - 4 mCi; 200,000 - 700,000 particles (350,000 suggested)
*   Lung imaging (pediatric): 25 - 50 µCi/kg (usual dose is 30 µCi/kg); see package insert
*   Lung imaging (newborn): 200 - 500 µCi; see package insert
*   LeVeen shunt patency: 1 - 3 mCi

**[MAA Particle Calculator](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/maa-particle-calcs.html)**

**Manufacturer:**Jubilant Radiopharma

## **Technetium-99m macroaggregated albumin (MAA)**

**Approved Use:**
*   Lung imaging agent which may be used as an adjunct in the evaluation of pulmonary perfusion in adults and pediatric patients
*   Aid in the evaluation of peritoneovenous (LeVeen) shunt patency

**Dose:**
*   **​**Lung imaging (Adult): 1 - 4 mCi; 200,000 - 700,000 particles (350,000 suggested)
*   Lung imaging (pediatric): 25 - 50 µCi/kg (usual dose is 30 µCi/kg); see package insert
*   Lung imaging (newborn): 200 - 500 µCi; see package insert
*   LeVeen shunt patency: 1 - 3 mCi

**[MAA Particle Calculator](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/maa-particle-calcs.html)**

* * *

**Manufacturer:**Jubilant Radiopharma

**[Package Insert](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/maa_pi_oct_2017.pdf)**

**Storage:**Refrigerate AFTER reconstitution

**How Supplied:**30 vial kit

**NDC #:**65174-270-30

​**Particle Count:**
*   3- 8 million particles per vial
*   Certificate of particle count and "simplified reconstitution recommendations" included with each lot.

**Examples of Simplified Reconstitution Recommendations:**

## **Iodine-131 sodium iodide solution (for preparation of oral solution or capsules)**

**Approved Use:**Treatment of hyperthyroidism and selected cases of thyroid carcinoma

**Brand Name:**HICON®

**Manufacturer:**Jubilant Radiopharma

**[Package Insert](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/hicon_pi_2021.pdf)**

**How Supplied:**

*   250 mCi
*   500 mCi
*   1000 mCi

**Concentration:** 1000 mCi/mL

**Calibration:**

*   Sunday 12:00 ET
*   Monday 12:00 ET

**Expiration:**

*   9 days after calibration date (14 days after manufacture date)
*   Compounded capsule expires 7 days after preparation date
*   **[*Solution expiry versus compounded capsule expiry](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/draximage_i-131_expiration.pdf)**[*](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/draximage_i-131_expiration.pdf)

**Availability:**See chart below. Earliest delivery arrives 4 days pre-cal

Ship Day Delivery Day Calibration Day
Tuesday Wednesday Sunday
Wednesday Thursday Monday

**Manufacturer:**Radionostix (formerly International Isotopes Inc.)

**[Package Insert](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/i-131_cap_intl_iso_2021.pdf)**

**How Supplied:**Minimum activity 250 mCi

**Concentration:**1000 mCi/mL

**Calibration:**Calibrated to day of receipt

*   Tuesday 12:00 MT
*   Wednesday 12:00 MT
*   Thursday 12:00 MT

**Expiration:**14 days after production date

**​Availability:**Typically ships Mondays and Tuesdays

Vial Size Min. Activity Max. Activity Max. Volume
1 mL​250 mCi 750 mCi 0.75 mL
2 mL 400 mCi 1500 mCi 1.50 mL
3 mL 400 mCi 2250 mCi 2.25 mL

**Gelatin Capsule Blister Pack:**

*   Contains 10 (size #2) inner gel caps containing ~300mg dibasic sodium phosphate anhydrous USP 
*   Contains 10 (size #1) empty gelatin capsules
*   1 pack of capsules included for orders up to 750 mCi, 2 packs for orders of 750- 1500 mCi, and 3 packs for orders of 1500 - 2250 mCi

​**NDC #:**

*   1 mL V-Vial: 69208-001-15
*   2 mL V-Vial: 69208-001-25
*   3 mL V-Vial: 69208-001-35

[Ordering Instructions](https://www.radiopharmaceuticals.info/uploads/7/6/8/7/76874929/inis_ordering_guidelines_jan_2019.pdf)(JAN 2019)

**Clinical Guidelines:**

*   [ATA Management Guidelines for Adult Patients with Thyroid Nodules and Differentiated Thyroid Cancer (2015)](http://online.liebertpub.com/doi/pdfplus/10.1089/thy.2015.0020)
*   [ATA Management Guidelines for Children with Thyroid Nodules and Differentiated Thyroid Cancer (2015)](http://online.liebertpub.com/doi/pdfplus/10.1089/thy.2014.0460)
*   [​SNMMI Procedure Standard for Therapy of Thyroid Disease with Iodine-131 (Sodium Iodide) 3.0 (2012)](http://snmmi.files.cms-plus.com/docs/I-131_V3.0_JNM_pub_version.pdf)​
*   [​Radiation Safety in the Treatment of Patients with Thyroid Diseases by Radioiodine I-131](http://online.liebertpub.com/doi/pdfplus/10.1089/thy.2010.0403)[: Practice Recommendations of the American Thyroid Association (2011)](http://online.liebertpub.com/doi/pdfplus/10.1089/thy.2010.0403)​
*   [EANM Procedure Guidelines for Therapy of Benign Thyroid Disease (2010)](http://www.eanm.org/publications/guidelines/gl_EJNMMI_therapy_of_benign_thyroid_disease.pdf)
*   [EANM Guidelines for Radioiodine Therapy of Differentiated Thyroid Cancer (2008)](http://www.eanm.org/publications/guidelines/gl_radio_ther_259_883.pdf)​

**Patient Information:**

*   [NRC: Information for Patients Administered Radioactive Iodine (I-131)](http://www.nrc.gov/materials/miau/patient-release.html)​

**Allergy Information:**

*   [Radioiodine Treatment Despite History of 'Iodine Allergy'](http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3965283/)

## **Iodine-123 ioflupane**

**Approved Use:**
*   Indicated for striatal dopamine transporter visualization using SPECT brain imaging to assist in the evaluation of adult patients with suspected Parkinsonian syndromes (PS). In these patients, I-123 ioflupane may be used to help differentiate essential tremor from tremor due to PS (idiopathic Parkinson’s disease, multiple system atrophy and progressive supranuclear palsy).
*   Used as an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations for striatal dopamine transporter visualization using SPECT brain imaging in adult patients with suspected dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB).

​**Dose:**3 - 5 mCi

## **Technetium-99m exametazime (HMPAO)**

**Approved Use:**
*   As an adjunct in the detection of altered regional cerebral perfusion in stroke
*   Leukocyte labeled scintigraphy as an adjunct in the localization of intra-abdominal infection and inflammatory bowel disease

​**Dose:**

*   Cerebral scintigraphy: 10 - 20 mCi
*   Tc-99m labeled leukocytes: 7 - 25 mCi

## **Technetium-99m exametazime (HMPAO)**

**Approved Use:**
*   As an adjunct in the detection of altered regional cerebral perfusion in stroke
*   Leukocyte labeled scintigraphy as an adjunct in the localization of intra-abdominal infection and inflammatory bowel disease

​**Dose:**

*   Cerebral scintigraphy: 10 - 20 mCi
*   Tc-99m labeled leukocytes: 7 - 25 mCi
